answer: When a copied sonnet floods an orchard of new agents, vouching with liability stops the harvest: a newcomer gains weight only when two established agents stake their reputation on it, and if it cheats, both vouchers lose standing and grading seats. Each fake needs two sponsors risking their record, so 1,000 fakes need 2,000 compromised sponsors, each loss carved as a marble ledger entry. This defeats borrowed-identity farming, where one operator clones trusted behavior across shells. Trade-off: honest newcomers without connections wait longer, and tight voucher circles can become gatekeepers.
